questions.question: What is the expected major product when Ethylene (H2C=CH2) is treated with Hydrogen bromide (HBr)?
questions.explanation: Treating Ethylene (H2C=CH2) with Hydrogen bromide (HBr) yields Bromoethane (CH3CH2Br). Rationale: Electrophilic attack of H+ forms an ethyl carbocation, followed by bromide nucleophilic capture.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Propene (CH3CH=CH2) into 1-Bromopropane (CH3CH2CH2Br)?
questions.explanation: To convert Propene (CH3CH=CH2) into 1-Bromopropane (CH3CH2CH2Br), the appropriate reagent is HBr / Peroxides (ROOR). Rationale: Bromine radical adds to the terminal carbon to form the more stable secondary carbon radical.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when tert-Butyl cation ((CH3)3C+) is treated with Water (H2O) then deprotonation?
questions.explanation: Treating tert-Butyl cation ((CH3)3C+) with Water (H2O) then deprotonation yields tert-Butanol ((CH3)3COH) + H3O+. Rationale: Nucleophilic attack of water on the planar carbocation yields an oxonium ion that loses a proton.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of tert-Butanol ((CH3)3COH) into 2-Methylpropene ((CH3)2C=CH2) + H2O?
questions.explanation: To convert tert-Butanol ((CH3)3COH) into 2-Methylpropene ((CH3)2C=CH2) + H2O, the appropriate reagent is Concentrated H2SO4 / heat. Rationale: Protonation, loss of water to form 3° carbocation, and subsequent beta-elimination yields isobutene.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when 1-Chlorobutane is treated with Sodium iodide (NaI) in acetone?
questions.explanation: Treating 1-Chlorobutane with Sodium iodide (NaI) in acetone yields 1-Iodobutane + NaCl precipitate. Rationale: Precipitation of insoluble NaCl drives the SN2 displacement of chloride by iodide.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Neopentyl iodide ((CH3)3CCH2I) into 2-Methyl-2-butanol (major rearrangement product)?
questions.explanation: To convert Neopentyl iodide ((CH3)3CCH2I) into 2-Methyl-2-butanol (major rearrangement product), the appropriate reagent is Ag+ / H2O. Rationale: Ionization forms the 1° neopentyl cation, which rapidly rearranges via 1,2-methyl shift to a stable 3° carbocation.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with Collision in gas phase to yield Butane (CH3CH2CH2CH3) as the major product?
questions.explanation: Two ethyl radicals (2 •CH2CH3) reacts with Collision in gas phase to yield Butane (CH3CH2CH2CH3). Rationale: Combination of two radical intermediates produces a neutral alkane chain with no free radicals remaining.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Triphenylmethyl cation (Ph3C+) is treated with Cycloheptatriene?
questions.explanation: Treating Triphenylmethyl cation (Ph3C+) with Cycloheptatriene yields Triphenylmethane (Ph3CH) + Tropylium cation (C7H7+). Rationale: Hydride transfer generates the exceptionally stable aromatic tropylium carbocation.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with Potassium hydroxide (KOH) in ethanol / heat to yield Ethylene (H2C=CH2) + KBr + H2O as the major product?
questions.explanation: Bromoethane (CH3CH2Br) reacts with Potassium hydroxide (KOH) in ethanol / heat to yield Ethylene (H2C=CH2) + KBr + H2O. Rationale: Strong base removes a beta-hydrogen concerted with bromide expulsion to form a double bond.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Propene (CH3CH=CH2) is treated with Cl2 in CH2Cl2?
questions.explanation: Treating Propene (CH3CH=CH2) with Cl2 in CH2Cl2 yields 1,2-Dichloropropane. Rationale: Chloronium ion formation followed by chloride backside opening yields the vicinal dichloride.
